01 / Parallel research

Four specialists. No single point of view.

Each analyst receives the same company and a narrow mandate. They work in parallel, cite what matters, and return a scored brief the debate agents can challenge.

AGENT / 01

Fundamentals

Reads filings, earnings, unit economics, capital allocation, and valuation. Separates durable improvement from a favorable quarter.

Filings · transcripts · estimates
AGENT / 02

Breaking news

Tracks fresh catalysts, policy shifts, supply-chain events, management changes, and what the market may not have priced yet.

News · releases · events
AGENT / 03

Social signal

Measures narrative velocity and crowding without confusing attention for truth. Flags sharp changes, echo chambers, and retail heat.

Feeds · forums · search trends
AGENT / 04

Price action

Reads trend, relative strength, liquidity, volatility, and key levels. Translates a sound thesis into the market’s actual behavior.

Price · volume · volatility
02 / Adversarial review

The thesis has to survive an argument.

The bull agent constructs the strongest evidence-based case for owning the asset. The bear agent is paid to break it—challenging assumptions, surfacing missing variables, and mapping the fastest path to permanent loss.

01
Shared evidence, opposed mandatesBoth agents see the same research so disagreements reveal interpretation—not missing context.
02
Explicit invalidationEvery recommendation states which observable fact would make the thesis wrong.
03
Steelman before synthesisThe final judge must summarize the strongest version of both sides before scoring the trade.
Evidence qualityConviction after challenge
Bull agent

03 / Governed execution

Ideas do not become positions by enthusiasm alone.

The chain separates analysis, execution, risk, and portfolio fit. Each handoff has a specific decision right, and risk can stop the process entirely.

Handoff / 01

Trade planner

Defines entry logic, order type, sizing bands, time horizon, and the exact level that invalidates the setup.

Handoff / 02

Risk gate

Stress-tests gaps, correlation, liquidity, concentration, and drawdown. It can resize, delay, or veto—without appeal.

Handoff / 03

Portfolio manager

Checks whether the idea improves the whole book, not just whether it looks attractive in isolation.

Handoff / 04

Decision ledger

Freezes the thesis, evidence, dissent, sizing, and expected path before hindsight can rewrite the story.

04 / Persistent memory

Every recommendation becomes training data.

The system snapshots each call, then grades it against the price path and the reasoning that produced it. Agents learn whether they were right for the right reason—and which signals repeatedly led them astray.

05 / The build guide

Build the desk in five deliberate layers.

Start with structured evidence and governance. Add autonomy only after you can audit how each decision was made.

01

Define one contract

Make every analyst return the same fields: claim, evidence, source, confidence, disconfirming evidence, and timestamp. This keeps synthesis measurable instead of conversational.

02

Fan out the research

Run fundamentals, news, sentiment, and technical analysis in parallel. Give each agent a narrow source policy and require citations for any claim that affects the score.

03

Force the debate

Provide both sides the same evidence bundle. Ask the bull to build the case, the bear to identify failure modes, and a judge to score what survives cross-examination.

04

Separate decision rights

The trader proposes execution. Risk owns veto and size caps. The portfolio manager signs off on correlation and opportunity cost. Log every override.

05

Close the learning loop

Store the point-in-time recommendation, then grade direction, magnitude, drawdown, timing, and thesis accuracy. Feed recurring mistakes back into prompts and thresholds.

Take the operating blueprint

Copy the role map, shared output contract, approval rules, and memory schema as a structured starter.

Build a system that remembers why it believed.
Research quality improves when decisions are challenged before the trade and examined after it.
